subject: SIG addendum: offline patch deliveries & support model for Atlas Bank
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Bank Compliance <compliance@atlasbank.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SIG addendum covering offline updates / evidence flow for on-prem deployment

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Compliance asked us to get a short SIG addendum that spells out how Redwood will handle: offline patch/agent updates, signed delivery of artifacts, and the support model for air-gapped on-prem nodes. Key asks from my side:

- Confirmation of delivery options (encrypted physical media vs. hand-carried signed artifact bundle)
- Artifact signing and verification process (how we can validate integrity)
- Evidence / attestation cadence (what artifacts/logs we will provide and how)
- Support hours, escalation path, and turnaround for emergency patches

We have a 12/22 internal compliance review; if we can get a draft addendum and any proof artifacts this week that would be ideal.

Can you assign who will own the draft and whether Redwood recommends a retainer for faster emergency turnarounds?

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Information Security Manager
Atlas Bank

--
Attachments: none
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG addendum covering offline updates / evidence flow for on-prem deployment

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I'm happy to own the addendum draft and coordinate across eng + security. High-level approach (proposal):

1) Delivery options (pick one or more)
   - Option A: Signed, encrypted artifact bundle shipped on hardware (e.g., AES-256 LUKS on SSD) via vetted courier; manifest and SHA-256 checksums provided before shipment.
   - Option B: Signed transportable package (signed with Redwood HSM-backed key) delivered on encrypted USB/signed manifest; customer performs onboard verification tooling we provide.
   - Option C: Remote staging via dedicated physical gateway (customer-run) where the update is staged by Redwood but fetched by customer on request (this is heavier to set up).

2) Signing/verification
   - All artifacts are signed with our HSM-protected key; we provide signed manifests (SHA-256) and a verification script (Python, single-file) the customer can run offline.

3) Evidence and attestation
   - For each offline update we can provide: signed manifest, package checksum, signed delivery receipt (courier chain-of-custody pdf), and a post-installation verification report (hashes + agent self-checks).
   - Frequency: per-delivery + quarterly attestation summary (unless requested more frequently).

4) Support model
   - Standard: business-hours remote support + triage for install instructions.
   - Premium retainer (recommended for banks): 24/7 emergency callback + guaranteed 4-hour triage window for emergency patches, plus on-call engineer allocation for packaging.

I'm attaching a first-draft runbook (offline_update_runbook_v2.md) that covers the artifact structure and verification steps. Can Karthik and Marissa confirm technical feasibility and how this maps to our SLA/retainer options?

If that looks good I will package a short SIG addendum (1–2 pages) we can send to your compliance team for review.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

--
Attachments: offline_update_runbook_v2.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG addendum - commercial + retainer note

Grace + team — quick commercial note from my side. Atlas is a strategic target; I'd recommend we present both:

- A no-cost standard addendum (covers artifact signing, checksums, and per-delivery evidence)
- An optional Premium Support Retainer (monthly) that includes guaranteed 4-hour emergency triage, prioritized packaging, and two annual on-site windows for artifact handover if requested.

Pricing pointers: for banks at this scale we typically price the retainer as a fixed monthly fee tied to a named on-call engineer and guaranteed response SLA. I'll draft suggested language for SOW if Grace wants me to.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: support_escalation_matrix.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T14:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG addendum: offline patch deliveries & support model for Atlas Bank

Thanks — technical comments below.

- Signing: we will sign packages with our HSM-managed key (PKCS#11). We can provide signed manifests and public key fingerprints for Atlas to store locally.
- Verification: the verification script in the runbook will run entirely offline; it returns a zero/non-zero exit code and a short JSON summary (hashes, signature verification, package version). We'll keep the script simple and dependency-free.
- Packaging: packages will be deterministic tar.gz with a versioned manifest (manifest.json) and a signature file (manifest.json.sig).
- Emergency patch flow:
   1) Triage via dedicated Slack/email for retainer customers.
   2) Build & sign hotfix bundle.
   3) Provide courier manifest + chain-of-custody PDF.
   4) Remote verification guide and follow-up verification run.

Constraints / notes:
- We cannot ship any builds that include third-party closed-source binaries without prior export and legal review.
- For checksum verification, we will use SHA-256. If Atlas requires SHA-512, we can support that but need to update the runbook.

I'll attach a short checklist we use internally for on-prem builds; Grace, if you want I can convert this to a one-page appendix to the SIG addendum.

-Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: (internal) onprem_packaging_checklist.md
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasbank.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Final: SIG addendum draft and evidence deliverables

Hi Sarah — attaching the SIG addendum draft (SIG_Addendum_AtlasBank_v1.1.pdf) and the final runbook excerpt. Highlights:

- Addendum is intentionally concise: definitions, delivery options (A/B/C), signing & verification details, evidence list (manifest, chain-of-custody, post-install report), and proposed acceptance criteria.
- Recommended acceptance: customer runs verification script post-install and returns a hash-matched signature report within 5 business days.
- Retainer language is provided as an appendix with suggested SLAs (4-hour triage, 8-hour patch delivery packaging time for emergencies, 2 annual on-site windows).

Next steps I propose:
1) Atlas reviews and provides any non-negotiable controls by 12/22 (per your timeline).
2) If acceptable, we issue the DocuSign envelope for countersignature (link below).
3) We then coordinate a quick run-through session for Atlas ops to walk the verification script (we recommend a 60-min dry-run).

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.com/envelope/example/ds123456
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/67890

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Final: SIG addendum draft and evidence deliverables

Thanks Hannah — this looks comprehensive and aligns with what compliance asked for. A few quick items:

- Compliance will review the addendum and runbook by 12/22 and come back with any clarifications.
- Please separate the retainer SOW language into a standalone draft (we prefer to review commercial terms separately).
- We'll need the verification script packaged as a single executable (Python + PyInstaller or small container) so our ops can run it without internet. Can you confirm delivery format?

Once we get the DocuSign envelope I'll route to our legal. Also — can we schedule a 60-minute dry run the week of 12/27? Prefer morning PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Information Security Manager
Atlas Bank
